niche.habitat: Photospheric flux tubes anchoring in umbrae; extends into granular upflows
niche.diet: Astrophage swarms and kinetic energy from granular plasma currents
niche.active: Constant; anchors deeply and filters the boiling photosphere

body: A self-organized helical plasma braid (Tsytovich & Morfill 2007) with lattice-reinforced filaments. One end is a super-dense magnetic knot embedded in a sunspot flux tube; the upper body fans into grapple-filaments that reach into adjacent granule upflows. The helix distributes torsional strain from differential rotation.

links: Differential rotation winds flux tubes over time

skill.effect: Reduces所受 damage by 60% and resists displacement for 5s by tightening the helix against the flux tube.

chains.weakness: Slow to reconfigure; rapid magnetic reorganization can snap the braid if anchored too tightly.
observe: The creature forms a distinct right-handed helix.
Filaments grip the glowing plasma of a granule upflow.
The anchor knot glows dimly in the umbra dark.

journal.en: It doesn't just live in the field; it argues with it, braid by braid, holding its ground against the star's spin.

plausibility.summary: Frame the body as a flux-rope-scale (≈10³ km, spot–granule junction) actively maintained dusty-plasma helix inside a closed tube, not a rigid braid. Tie Braid Lock to tightening linkage around the anchor knot and diamagnetic stiffening (F16) rather than ignoring reconnection; weakness on tight anchor + fast reorganization stays honest.

analogues.organism: No Earth organism resists stellar-scale torsion in plasma. Closest parallels: (1) solar magnetic flux ropes / prominences (helical field-supported plasma structures; Berger & Prior 2006, Roy Soc. Proc. A); (2) supercoiled DNA and flagellar filaments distributing torsional strain in biology (mechanism unrelated to MHD, but selection for twist management is real).

journal.en: The star boils, and the Trenza drinks the heat off the boil, siphoning motion into structure.

plausibility.summary: Rebrand Siphon Grasp as harvesting Astrophage enriched in upflow plumes plus coupling to magnetoacoustic perturbations in the plume (7–10 km/s regime F7), with healing tied to captured prey's energy budget (F15, F22), not wholesale theft of convective kinetic energy from the granule.

journal.en: It speaks in waves, and the star's magnetic skin carries its voice across the dark.

Secret ‘sing back’ low-frequency hum → coordinate prediction: tie to torsional oscillation / emerging flux timing (F4, F2) with 10 s lead time as speculative helioseismic-style coupling, labeled highly speculative.

For wave-based herd control on a conductor, lightning-related Schumann resonances are a poor fit—better game analogy is elephants’ infrasonic communication through ground, but medium here is MHD on a flux tube.

relations.note: (council kind 'Predator') Trenza filters and consumes Astrophage swarms to prevent overgrowth on its filaments; the Astrophage gain mobility by riding Trenza's updrafts.
(council kind 'Competitor') Remo steals Astrophage from Trenza's filaments using speed; Trenza occasionally traps Remo in siphon-grasps.

temperament: Stolid, territorial, slow to release grip
secrets: If you play a low-frequency Alfvén hum near a Trenza, it will 'sing back', revealing its precise magnetic coordinate and allowing you to predict the next reconnection event within 10 seconds.
moments: A solar flare strikes. The Trenza does not flee. Its helix locks, the lattice skin scatters the initial UV blast, and for ten seconds, the creature becomes a beacon, braiding the reconnection field lines into its own structure, growing in mass and complexity as the flare dies, a living knot in the star's wound.

journal.en: It is the anchor and the filter, the slow mind in the boiling sea.
You cannot blow it away; you must convince the magnetic field to let go.
